title: Schema Change Recovery
content:
## Symptoms
A schema-change incident may cause unresolved column errors, missing column errors, type mismatch failures, or unexpected null values after an upstream producer changes its contract.

## Diagnosis
Compare the previous and current schemas. Identify added, removed, renamed, or type-changed columns. Review recent upstream deployments and verify whether the producer communicated a contract change.

## Impact Analysis
Check data lineage to identify downstream Silver, Gold, reporting, and machine-learning workloads depending on the changed fields.

## Recovery
Update the transformation mapping only after confirming the intended source change. Validate the modified transformation against affected data, rerun the failed partition or batch, and avoid blindly rerunning downstream jobs before validation.

## Validation
Verify row counts, schema compatibility, null rates, duplicate counts, and downstream outputs before marking the incident resolved.

## Prevention
Introduce schema contracts, compatibility validation, producer-consumer communication, and pre-production schema checks.

title: Duplicate Data Recovery
content:
## Symptoms
Duplicate transaction counts increase after a pipeline failure or retry.

## Diagnosis
Determine whether the previous execution partially committed data before failing. Check batch identifiers, transaction keys, retry history, and affected partitions.

## Recovery
Quarantine the affected partition. Deduplicate using the stable business key. Replace or merge the corrected data and rerun the failed batch using idempotent write logic.

## Validation
Compare source and target counts, validate duplicate counts, and confirm downstream aggregates before releasing the pipeline.

## Prevention
Use idempotent MERGE logic, batch identifiers, transactional writes, and safe retry mechanisms.
